chunks: Muhammad ibn Umar al-Hafiz al-Baghdadi narrated that Abu Muhammad Al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Momatta’ quoted on the authority of Hamdan ibn al-Mokhtar, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Khalid al-Barqi, on the authority of his Master Abu Ja’far Muhammad ibn Ali (s), on the authority of his father Ali ibn Musa Al-Ridha (s), on the authority of his father Musa ibn Ja’far (s), on the authority of al-Ajlah al-Kendi, on the authority of Abi Borayda’, on the authority of his father that God’s Prophet (s) said, “Ali is the Divine Leader for all the believers after me.”

key_terms.أَهْلُ الْبَيْتِ: The People of the House, referring to the Prophet's family and Imams.
key_terms.إِمَامُ: Leader or guide, specifically referring to the divinely appointed successor in Shia theology.
key_terms.بَعْدِي: After me, indicating succession following the Prophet's death or lifetime.
key_terms.صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَآلِهِ: Peace be upon him and his family, a common honorific for the Prophet.
key_terms.مُؤْمِنٍ: Believer, referring to the community of faithful followers.

ai.seo_question: What did the Prophet Muhammad say about Ali's role after him?
ai.summary: Recorded by Shaykh al-Saduq in *Uyun Akhbar al-Rida*, this hadith features a prestigious chain (isnad) linking Imam Ali al-Rida directly to the Prophet, emphasizing the divine appointment (Nass) of Imam Ali ibn Abi Talib as the successor to all believers. It serves as a critical proof for the Shia doctrine of Imamate, reinforcing the continuity of spiritual and political authority within the Ahl al-Bayt.
